primitives.name: Hip Placement Optimization
primitives.verbatim_quote: The ball should always be passed at the outside hip and just ahead of the runner.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'d_hip': "distance from runner's hip to pass point (meters)", 'v_runner': "runner's velocity (m/s)", 't_pass': 'time between pass initiation and reception (seconds)'}
primitives.assumptions: Runner maintains constant velocity; pass is instantaneous; hip alignment is optimal for acceleration.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When d_hip < 0.1 m, runner decelerates due to misalignment.

layer2.mapping: Optimal hip placement minimizes receiver deceleration and maximizes forward momentum transfer through vector alignment.
layer2.telemetry: Receiver acceleration vector deviation from intended path

primitives.name: Pass Velocity Kinematics
primitives.verbatim_quote: The quarter should get the ball to the runner instantly and then get into the interference himself.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'v_pass': 'pass velocity (m/s)', 't_instant': 'instantaneous pass delivery time (s)', 'F_interference': 'interference force magnitude (N)'}
primitives.assumptions: Instantaneous pass delivery implies minimal delay; interference is modeled as a scalar force.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When t_instant > 0.2 s, receiver loses positional advantage.

layer2.mapping: Pass velocity kinematics mirror receiver positioning dynamics in a dual-time-space transformation.
layer2.telemetry: Time-to-reception variance and interference impact on pass accuracy

primitives.name: Catching Reliability Model
primitives.verbatim_quote: The oblong shape of the ball and the fact that it is inflated with air makes its flight uncertain to some extent, yet with practice a player can learn to judge just where the ball will fall and to be there in the proper place to receive it.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'σ_flight': 'flight uncertainty standard deviation (meters)', 't_learn': 'learning time (seconds)', 'P_catch': 'probability of successful catch (dimensionless)'}
primitives.assumptions: Flight trajectory follows Gaussian distribution; learning improves prediction accuracy linearly.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When σ_flight > 0.5 m, catch probability drops below 0.6.

layer2.mapping: Catch reliability emerges from stochastic flight modeling and predictive positioning convergence.
layer2.telemetry: Catch success rate over repeated trials and wind condition variations

Hip placement directly influences the runner’s acceleration vector, with optimal alignment ensuring maximum forward momentum. Pass velocity must be synchronized with receiver timing to avoid delays that lead to interception. The kinematic model of pass delivery is a function of time-to-reception and interference dynamics. Catching reliability is a probabilistic outcome influenced by aerodynamic uncertainty and learned predictive behavior. These primitives form a closed-loop system where each element—passing precision, receiver timing, and catch reliability—mutually reinforces or degrades performance. Failure modes include misaligned hip targeting causing deceleration, delayed passes enabling defensive counterplay, and unpredictable ball trajectories reducing catch probability. The system exhibits emergent properties such as team-wide coordination efficiency and strategic adaptability to environmental factors like wind. Dualities arise in the symmetry between offensive pass initiation and defensive coverage strategies, where each action triggers a corresponding counter-action. The mathematical framework supports both deterministic optimization and stochastic resilience modeling.
